211 EOK OUTREACH COORDINATOR

Reports to: 211 EOK Executive Director

ABOUT TULSA AREA UNITED WAY

Tulsa Area United Way (TAUW) unites people and resources to improve lives and strengthen communities. Since 1924, TAUW has raised and invested nearly $925 million to assist people in need in Creek, Okmulgee, Osage, Rogers, Wagoner, and Tulsa counties. TAUW, along with our Nonprofit Partners, community collaboration initiatives, social innovation grants, and support for the 160 programs within our nonprofit community, work to advance the common good by focusing on the four pillars of a better quality of life – healthy community, youth opportunities, financial security, and community resilience. Thousands of amazing volunteers, hundreds of companies, and area leaders partner with our great team to stay focused on the mission of uniting people and resources to improve lives and strengthen our communities.

Our team members enjoy a flexible work environment, built on transparency, trust, and community stewardship. We offer a competitive total rewards package. Visit our website at tauw.org to learn more.

ROLE OF THE 211 EOK OUTREACH COORDINATOR

This position represents 211 Eastern Oklahoma, a free service connecting individuals across

37 counties in Eastern Oklahoma to vital community resources via phone, live chat, text,

or online search. The role has two key functions: growing awareness for 211 EOK

and helping to find resources to add to the database in the assigned area. The position

requires building collaborative relationships with stakeholders, United Ways, and Information

and Referral programs while supporting outreach and community activities. This position

requires extensive local travel across the assigned counties.

CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

Outreach, Awareness and Education

  • Identify and cultivate new relationships with community groups, corporations and nonprofits to educate about 211 EOK.
  • Create and implement strategies to initiate contacts and build relationships.
  • Attend meetings and deliver presentations to inform partners and clients of agency value and build partnerships.
  • Coordinate ongoing outreach and training to top service providers and key community groups.
  • Document all interactions in software platforms to support follow-up and program planning

Resource Gathering

  • Analyze service gaps and identify new partners or opportunities for collaboration
  • Communicate with Database Curator Team to ensure that resource partner information is current, accurate and complete.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education and Experience

  • High School diploma or GED required (preference for advanced skill sets, equivalent experience, or 211-specific certification)
  • Prior experience in program outreach or similar position preferred
  • Knowledge of database systems and experience with data gathering, categorizing, and analysis preferred
  • Direct Services and/or Information and referral experience preferred
  • Exceptional attention to detail, responsiveness, and customer service
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Outlook, Excel)
  • Strong organizational, time management, and communication skills
  • Problem-solving and critical thinking abilities
  • Ability to manage priorities in a fast-paced environment independently and as part of a team.

Working Conditions

  • Day-to-day work will be conducted primarily remote with occasional office or team meetings conducted in-person. The ability to work remotely requires trust and confidence from the Leadership Team. You must have proven abilities to work independently with little to no guidance from management.
  • Extensive local travel required (milage will be reimbursed at the current IRS rate)
  • TAUW hosts multiple events throughout the year where attendance is required and are held in both indoor and outdoor locations.

Job Description Summary

‎

Under the direction of Burden of Illness department leadership, the Risk Adjustment Coding Specialist is responsible for various aspects of decision-making and coding reviews to facilitate, obtain, validate, and reconcile appropriate provider documentation for clinical conditions that accurately reflect the severity of illness and complexity of patient care.

‎

How will you make an impact & Requirements

‎

This position is responsible for risk adjustment coding and quality assurance validation for the following programs, including but not limited to:

  • Prospective medical record review
  • Concurrent outpatient claim diagnosis coding
  • Retrospective medical record and provider response reviews

Responsibilities

Perform prospective medical record reviews for clinical indicators supportive of an underlying diagnosis to be presented to a clinician for review during a subsequent face-to-face encounter.

  • Review the encounter level patient medical record and provider selected ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes in real time prior to claim submission to validate completeness and accuracy of provider selected ICD-10-CM codes.
  • Collaborate with healthcare providers and other stakeholders to clarify documentation and ensure accurate coding and reporting of diagnoses.
  • Stay updated on changes to Medicare guidelines, coding regulations, and reimbursement methodologies to ensure compliance and accuracy in coding practices.
  • Participate in coding education and training initiatives for staff to promote consistent and accurate coding practices across the organization.
  • Stays current on applicable coding and documentation guideline changes and rules.
  • This role is expected to maintain a consistent accuracy rate of 95% or higher and able to meet productivity standards established by leadership.
  • Perform other job-related duties as assigned by leadership.
  • Abstract and assign ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes supported in the encounter documentation not initially assigned to the encounter claim following ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting.
  • Conduct retrospective audits of medical records to validate the accuracy and completeness of diagnosis coding and claim submission, identifying and resolving any discrepancies or areas for improvement.
  • Perform comprehensive reviews of provider actions within the Value Based Alert Tool (VBAT) to identify outliers and areas of opportunity.
  • Analyze MRA data to identify patterns and when requested assist in the development of interventions at the provider and region level.
  • Keeps department leadership apprised of project activities through regular written and oral status reports. Proactively identifies risks that may hinder project success.
  • May be assigned additional projects/higher work volume than Risk Adjustment Coding Specialist I

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED equivalent
  • Current active coding credential through AAPC or AHIMA required.
    • Preference given to those with CRC designation.
  • Maintains active professional certification and complies with all educational, professional, and ethical requirements of said certification.
  • Minimum of one (1) year of experience in medical field, preferably in an outpatient or accountable care organization setting.
  • Proficiency in ICD-10-CM coding guidelines and conventions.
  • Knowledge of medical terminology, abbreviations, anatomy and physiology, major disease processes, and pharmacology.
  • Familiarity of Medicare risk adjustment methodologies and HCC coding principles.
  • Excellent diligence and analytical skills, with the ability to review and interpret complex medical documentation.
  • Effective communication and people skills to collaborate with healthcare providers and other team members.
  • Ability to work independently and prioritize tasks to meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Proficiency in electronic health record (EHR) systems.
  • Commitment to maintaining confidentiality and adhering to ethical coding standards.

Level II (in addition to minimum qualifications):

  • Minimum of two (2) years coding experience or directly related medical experience, one (1) of which includes Hierarchical Condition Category (HCC) coding.
  • Advanced knowledge of medical terminology, abbreviations, anatomy and physiology, major disease processes, and pharmacology.
  • Extensive knowledge of coding conventions and payment rules as they apply to medical record documentation, billing of medical services, and health care reimbursement systems. This includes a comprehensive understanding of ICD-10-CM.
  • Advanced technical skills for use of MS Office (Excel, Word, Access, and PowerPoint).
  • Demonstrated ability to utilize a variety of electronic medical records systems.
  • Ability to manage significant workload, and to work efficiently under pressure meeting established deadlines with minimal supervision. Strong time management skills. Must possess high degree of accuracy, efficiency, and dependability.
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate clearly and effectively with a wide variety of individuals at all levels of the organization both verbally and written.
  • Demonstrated organizational and problem-solving ability.
  • Strong analytical and mathematical skills.
  • Demonstrated experience in project completion, educational program development and/or group presentation.

‎

$19.00

to

$28.50

Actual compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, skills, qualifications, geographic location, internal equity, and business needs.

Job Description Summary

‎

The Medical Economics Analyst I supports the organization's value-based (VB) contracts, including MSSP ACOs and Advantage, Commercial ACOs. This role performs defined and recurring analyses, supports reporting and dashboard development, validates data, and helps identify trends that inform cost, utilization, quality, risk adjustment, and shared savings performance.
Working under the guidance of more experienced Medical Economics team members, the Analyst I develops foundational knowledge of healthcare claims, EHR, risk adjustment, quality, attribution, and financial data. The role is expected to build strong technical skills, produce accurate and timely work, ask thoughtful questions, and progressively take ownership of routine analyses and reporting deliverables.

‎

How will you make an impact & Requirements

‎

Value-Based Analytics Support

  • Perform standard and recurring analyses for value-based contracts, including medical cost trends, utilization, risk score performance, quality metrics, and shared savings performance.
  • Prepare data pulls, recurring reports, provider-level summaries, and basic performance analyses using established methodologies and templates.
  • Identify notable trends, variances, or potential data issues and escalate findings to senior team members for review.
  • Support ad hoc analyses and special projects by gathering data, performing calculations, and documenting results.
  • Develop working knowledge of value-based program requirements, payer methodologies, benchmarks, and key performance measures.

Data & Technical Development

  • Write, modify, and troubleshoot SQL queries using established data models, tables, and coding standards.
  • Work with healthcare datasets including claims, EHR, risk adjustment, quality, and attribution data.
  • Perform routine data validation, reconciliation, and quality checks to confirm completeness and accuracy of analytical outputs.
  • Assist with recurring datasets, extracts, and reporting processes that support Medical Economics deliverables.
  • Document query logic, data sources, metric definitions, assumptions, and analytical steps to support consistency and reproducibility.
  • Partner with senior analysts or data engineering resources to investigate and resolve data discrepancies.

Reporting & Visualization

  • Build and maintain standard reports and dashboards in Tableau, Sigma, Excel, or other approved reporting tools using defined requirements.
  • Perform quality assurance on recurring dashboards and reports before distribution.
  • Create clear charts, tables, and summaries that communicate key findings to internal stakeholders.
  • Support automation and process-improvement efforts that reduce manual work and improve reporting consistency.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Collaborate with Medical Economics, Finance, Quality, Care Management, Population Health, Clinical Operations, and other internal teams to support analytical requests.
  • Participate in project and stakeholder meetings, communicate progress, and follow through on assigned action items.
  • Explain analytical results clearly and appropriately for the audience, with support from senior team members as needed.
  • Seek feedback, incorporate coaching, and contribute to team standards, documentation, and shared best practices.

This position is the primary processor for new student immigration processing, SEVIS record management, and serves as a liaison between prospective students, enrollment teams, and U.S. government agencies.

  • Lead communication efforts with enrollment management, admissions, and academic departments regarding international student immigration processes and requirements and provide training and guidance to enrollment team members on immigration regulations, documentation requirements, and best practices
  • Maintain current knowledge of F-1 visa regulations and other nonimmigrant visa categories (B-1/B-2, H-1B, L-1, O-1, etc.) to effectively advise students pursuing change of status applications
  • Assist students with complex immigration matters requiring coordination between multiple visa types
  • Uses AI tools to support daily work activities, enhance output quality, and improve efficiency within defined processes and guidelines

  • Thorough knowledge of SEVIS, SEVP regulations, and F-1 visa requirements
  • Strong understanding of U.S. immigration law and procedures
  • Excellent interpersonal and cross-cultural communication skills
  • Demonstrated ability to interpret and apply complex federal regulations
  • Strong organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment

Required Skills

  • Previous experience as a DSO or in international student services

Our collective future depends on carbon-free transportation. To forge that future, Voltera develops, owns, and operates the infrastructure that enables companies to succeed at scale with zero-emission vehicles. We’re looking for innovative, people-first team members who understand that culture is critical in our effort to positively impact the world’s transition to a carbon-free transportation future.

The Director, Integrated Operations Center (IOC) leads and scales Voltera's Integrated Operations Center as the company grows its network of public and autonomous vehicle charging sites. This role owns the customer relationship for live sites, serving as the single point of contact for issue intake, status, and resolution, and acts as the central command function during operational events.

This individual builds the org design, staffing model, and escalation frameworks that keep the IOC running at high service quality as the portfolio scales, while partnering closely with charging ops, facility ops, network ops, security, and technology.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

Org Design & Team Leadership

  • Lead and scale the IOC to support a growing portfolio of sites and customers.
  • Develop the org design and staffing model to support a rapidly expanding network while maintaining high service quality and cost discipline.

Customer Relationship & Issue Resolution

  • Own the customer relationship for live sites, serving as their single point of contact for issue intake, status, and resolution.
  • Lead cross-functional coordination during operational events, serving as the central command function across internal SMEs, customers, and external vendors.
  • Establish and manage escalation frameworks, routing operational issues to the appropriate internal SMEs, vendor partners, and executive stakeholders based on severity, business impact, and service-level commitments.

Process & Tooling

  • Create and continuously improve operational SOPs in close collaboration with charging ops, facility ops, network ops, and security.
  • Partner with the technology team to develop tooling and automation that improve the IOC's performance and customer experience.

Performance Management

  • Identify and develop measurement methodologies, then manage KPIs related to issue resolution.

MUST-HAVE:

  • 10+ years of experience in operations, command center, NOC/IOC, or customer-facing operational leadership, ideally in a fast-growing infrastructure, energy, or fleet environment.
  • Demonstrated experience building or scaling a 24/7 operations or support function, including org design, staffing models, and escalation frameworks.
  • Track record owning customer relationships in an operational context, including issue intake, status communication, and resolution.
  • Experience developing SOPs and cross-functional processes with multiple internal stakeholder groups.
  • Strong crisis/incident management skills, with the ability to serve as central command during live operational events.
  • Comfort defining and managing KPIs and partnering with technology teams to build supporting tooling.

NICE-TO-HAVE:

  • Experience in EV charging, AV/robotaxi, fleet operations, or broader energy infrastructure.
  • Experience working in a high-growth, fast-paced startup environment.
  • Familiarity with facilities operations, field service coordination, or vendor/SLA management.

LOCATION:

  • Flexible
  • Travel Expectations (as needed)

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Base compensation: $200,000 to $225,000 annually. Exact compensation may vary based on skills, experience, and location. Our total compensation package includes the base salary, bonus, incentive equity compensation, and competitive benefits (medical/vision/dental insurance, matching 401(k), Life Insurance, unlimited vacation/PTO, & EV incentive). Candidates must have authorization to work in the U.S. on a permanent basis. Relocation benefits are not available.

raw.description:
Buscamos un Representante Técnico de Ventas responsable del desarrollo comercial y la venta consultiva de soluciones de Reología y Calorimetría Diferencial de Barrido (DSC), con foco principal en Reología y una responsabilidad complementaria en análisis térmico por DSC.

Esta posición combina prospección, desarrollo de cuentas, calificación técnica, demostraciones y cierre de ventas. Buscamos un perfil claramente comercial, con capacidad para abrir mercado y suficiente base técnica para conversar con formuladores, investigadores, responsables de calidad, proceso, laboratorio, compras y dirección.

Responsabilidades principales

  • Desarrollar comercialmente el portafolio de Reología y DSC en el territorio asignado, dedicando la mayor parte del esfuerzo comercial a soluciones de Reología.
  • Prospectar y desarrollar nuevos clientes en sectores como pinturas y recubrimientos, polímeros, adhesivos, farmacéutica, cosmética, alimentos, químicos, petroquímicos, lubricantes, baterías, academia, I+D y control de calidad.
  • Gestionar el ciclo completo de venta: identificación de oportunidades, calificación técnica, presentación de soluciones, elaboración de propuestas, negociación y cierre.
  • Identificar aplicaciones reológicas relacionadas con viscosidad y curvas de flujo, esfuerzo de cedencia, tixotropía, viscoelasticidad, estabilidad de formulaciones y comportamiento dependiente del tiempo, temperatura y frecuencia.
  • Identificar oportunidades de DSC para caracterización de transiciones térmicas, temperatura de transición vítrea (Tg), fusión, cristalización, curado, estabilidad oxidativa, polimorfismo, compatibilidad y pureza, según la aplicación.
  • Realizar presentaciones técnico-comerciales y coordinar demostraciones de reómetros y calorímetros DSC, con apoyo de especialistas de aplicación cuando sea necesario.
  • Asesorar al cliente en la selección de la solución adecuada de acuerdo con muestra, formulación, proceso, rango de temperatura, método de prueba, nivel de automatización y objetivos de medición.
  • Desarrollar relaciones de largo plazo con formuladores, investigadores, responsables de laboratorio, calidad, I+D, producción, proceso, compras y tomadores de decisión.
  • Cumplir los objetivos de venta trimestrales y anuales, así como los indicadores comerciales definidos por la gerencia.
  • Mantener actualizado el CRM con oportunidades, actividades, forecast, seguimiento comercial y etapas del pipeline.
  • Identificar oportunidades de venta cruzada con otras líneas de producto de la compañía.
  • Dar seguimiento postventa para asegurar la satisfacción del cliente, fortalecer la relación y detectar nuevas oportunidades de negocio.
  • Participar en capacitaciones técnicas y comerciales, ferias, seminarios, workshops y eventos especializados en México y en el extranjero.
  • Formación profesional en Ingeniería Química, Química, Materiales, Polímeros, Alimentos, Farmacéutica, Mecánica, Mecatrónica, Física, Nanotecnología o carrera afín con base técnica sólida.
  • Mínimo 3 años de experiencia en ventas técnicas B2B, indispensable, preferentemente de instrumentación científica, equipos analíticos, equipos de laboratorio, reómetros, viscosímetros, análisis térmico o soluciones para formulación, I+D y control de calidad.
  • Se valorará especialmente experiencia comercial o de aplicaciones en Reología/Viscosimetría, o experiencia vendiendo instrumentación a industrias donde la formulación y el comportamiento de flujo sean variables críticas.
  • Experiencia comprobable en prospección, apertura de cuentas nuevas, desarrollo de oportunidades y construcción de pipeline; no buscamos un perfil limitado únicamente al mantenimiento de cuentas existentes.
  • Capacidad para comprender una necesidad técnica y convertirla en una propuesta comercial de valor, sin perder el enfoque en avance de oportunidad, negociación y cierre.
  • Habilidad para comunicarse con perfiles técnicos y no técnicos: formuladores, investigadores, ingenieros, responsables de calidad, producción, laboratorio, compras y dirección.
  • Perfil altamente orientado a resultados, con disciplina para el cumplimiento de objetivos y seguimiento sistemático de oportunidades.
  • Manejo de CRM/ERP, forecast y metodología de seguimiento comercial.
  • Disponibilidad para viajar frecuentemente dentro y fuera del país.
  • Manejo de automóvil y disponibilidad para traslados en carretera.
  • Inglés intermedio conversacional indispensable para capacitación y comunicación técnica.

Experiencia deseable

Se dará prioridad a candidatos con experiencia directa en Reología o Viscometría, aunque no cuenten todavía con experiencia específica en DSC.

  • Venta, aplicación o uso técnico de reómetros rotacionales/oscilatorios, viscosímetros de laboratorio o sistemas de caracterización de flujo y viscoelasticidad.
  • Desarrollo, formulación o control de calidad de pinturas, recubrimientos, tintas, adhesivos, asfaltos, cosméticos, productos farmacéuticos, alimentos o formulaciones químicas.
  • Pruebas reológicas como curvas de flujo, esfuerzo de cedencia, tixotropía, barridos de amplitud/frecuencia/temperatura, recuperación estructural, creep o relajación.
  • Caracterización de polímeros, elastómeros, resinas, materiales fundidos, slurries, suspensiones, emulsiones, geles, pastas o materiales para baterías.
  • Experiencia en análisis térmico, DSC, DMA, TGA o técnicas relacionadas será considerada un valor adicional, pero no es un requisito indispensable.
  • Conocimiento de aplicaciones de DSC en polímeros o farmacéutica, incluyendo Tg, fusión, cristalización, curado, estabilidad, polimorfismo o pureza.

La prioridad es encontrar un vendedor técnico fuerte en Reología. El conocimiento de DSC puede desarrollarse mediante entrenamiento técnico y acompañamiento de especialistas de aplicación

Soluciones y tecnologías de la línea

Deseable familiaridad con Reología; el conocimiento de DSC puede adquirirse durante el proceso de capacitación. Las tecnologías incluyen:

  • Reometría rotacional y oscilatoria para líquidos, semisólidos, dispersiones, emulsiones, geles, pastas y materiales complejos.
  • Medición de viscosidad, curvas de flujo, esfuerzo de cedencia, tixotropía, viscoelasticidad, creep, relajación y recuperación estructural.
  • Barridos de amplitud, frecuencia, tiempo y temperatura; control de fuerza normal y accesorios para aplicaciones avanzadas.
  • Sistemas de medición y accesorios para formulación, control de calidad, polímeros, reología de polvos, tribología y caracterización especializada, según aplicación.
  • Calorimetría Diferencial de Barrido para Tg, fusión, cristalización, curado, estabilidad oxidativa, capacidad calorífica y caracterización térmica de materiales.

​​​​​​​Ofrecemos

  • Sueldo competitivo.
  • Bono por desempeño y esquema de comisiones.
  • Prestaciones superiores a las de la ley.
  • Herramientas de trabajo: automóvil, laptop y celular corporativo.
  • Capacitación técnica y comercial continua en México y en el extranjero.
  • Desarrollo profesional dentro de una empresa internacional líder en instrumentación científica.

Job Description

Since 2000, Crum & Forster’s Accident & Health division (A&H) has offered a diverse portfolio of specialty insurance and reinsurance products nationwide. We place a strong focus on product development and creative distribution methods, along with excellent client service and support.

In addition to our robust domestic portfolio, which spans both special risk and medical solutions, A&H works on an international basis through various partnerships. Our global capabilities provide our partners with even broader flexibility in underwriting solutions.

At year-end 2024, the SBU recorded $982M in gross premium written.

About the Role, Line of Business, and Team:This senior-level position is part of the Accident & Health (A&H) Strategic Business Unit (SBU), specifically within the Special Risk team—a group focused on delivering tailored insurance solutions to a broad range of niche markets. The A&H Special Risk team manages a diverse and evolving portfolio of programs through partnerships with Managing General Underwriters (MGUs), Third Party Administrators (TPAs), and other key producers.

As an AVP, Underwriting Manager, you will play a critical leadership role in shaping the profitability, direction, and growth of the book. With a high degree of autonomy, you will be responsible for the strategic evaluation, selection, and management of complex risks, while serving as a key decision-maker on underwriting and program structure. You will lead high-level negotiations, provide oversight on reinsurance placements with Crum & Forster for other carriers, and offer guidance on technical underwriting matters across multiple specialty lines.

In addition to cultivating strong relationships with MGUs, producers, and internal stakeholders, you will help drive operational efficiency and innovation across the business. You will lead the onboarding of new MGA and TPA partners across multiple chassis and serve as a mentor and technical resource to junior team members. This role requires a forward-thinking, solution-oriented professional with deep market knowledge, proven underwriting acumen, and the ability to influence strategy and outcomes at both the account and portfolio levels.

What you will do:

  • Meet profitability, retention, and written premium goals determined by the department
  • Make independent decisions within underwriting letter of authority and maintain proper file documentation
  • Assist in developing annual business goals for assigned agents/producers
  • Responsible for analyzing results and maintaining accountability of agency partners within the department
  • Maintain awareness of market trends and identify emerging threats to the department
  • Has an in-depth knowledge of department products and services
  • Clearly articulate the department’s value proposition
  • May provide input into the development of strategic annual department planning activities
  • Perform Underwriting Audits
  • Lead, develop, motivate, and retain a high performing team or UW staff members. Proactively addresses concerns, holds team accountable, makes sound decisions, and sets clear direction
  • Attend any necessary due diligence review for new MGUs
  • Participates in training and initiatives
  • On boarding of new clients and/or new accounts
  • Manage the reinsurance relationships and the process
  • Other duties as assigned

What YOU will bring to C&F:

  • Possess strong problem-solving skills
  • Strong risk management and analytical skills
  • Excellent organizational and time management skills
  • Strong interpersonal skills necessary to interact with brokers, producers and clients
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Flexible and open to an ever changing, fast paced environment
  • Proven leadership ability
  • Exceptional attention to detail
  • Ability to multi-task with an emphasis on quality and customer service

Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university
  • 10+ years of underwriting experience required
  • Previous leadership experience
  • Underwrite submissions of quotes that may be applicable to the travel, travel medical and blanket accident business segments
  • Strong Microsoft Office skills, i.e. Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.
  • Travel required, 15-20%
  • Proficient in software needed to succeed in department
  • Possesses underwriting and industry designations applicable to SBU desired

What C&F will bring to you

At C&F you will BELONG

We value inclusivity and diversity. We are committed to equal employment opportunity and welcome everyone regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. If you require special accommodation, please let us know.

For California Residents Only: Information collected and processed as part of your career profile and any job applications you choose to submit are subject to our privacy notices and policies, visit for more information.

Crum & Forster is committed to ensuring a workplace free from discriminatory pay disparities and complying with applicable pay equity laws. Salary ranges are available for all positions at this location, taking into account roles with a comparable level of responsibility and impact in the relevant labor market and these salary ranges are regularly reviewed and adjusted in accordance with prevailing market conditions. The annualized base pay for the advertised position, located in the specified area, ranges from a minimum of $141,800 to a maximum of $208,000. The actual compensation is determined by various factors, including but not limited to the market pay for the jobs at each level, the responsibilities and skills required for each job, and the employee’s contribution (performance) in that role. To be considered within market range, a salary is at or above the minimum of the range. You may also have the opportunity to participate in discretionary equity (stock) based compensation and/or performance-based variable pay programs.

  • Flexible work arrangements.
  • Competitive compensation package.
  • Generous 401K employer match.
  • Employee Stock Purchase plan with employer matching.
  • Generous Paid Time Off.
  • Excellent benefits that go beyond health, dental & vision. Our Wellness programs focus on your family’s complete wellness, including your physical and mental wellbeing
  • A core C&F principle is that you manage your career. To support your development, we have a wealth of ways for you to keep learning, including tuition reimbursement, industry related certifications and professional training available to you.
  • A dynamic, ambitious, fun and exciting work environment.
  • A spirit of social responsibility, matching donation program, volunteer opportunities, and an employee driven corporate giving.

raw.title: Inbound Account Executive - Global, Remote (UNCAPPED COMMISSIONS)
raw.excerpt: About MagicMagic is a leading modern outsourcing platform that connects SMBs to high-quality remote workers, from SDRs to virtual assistants and more.
raw.description:
About Magic
Magic is a leading modern outsourcing platform that connects SMBs to high-quality remote workers, from SDRs to virtual assistants and more. With roots in Silicon Valley and backing from top venture capitalists, our workers are supercharged with a combination of the latest AI technology and training. We came out of Y Combinator in 2015, have grown to 1,000+ remote workers, and are backed by Sequoia Capital with over $30M in funding.

Background
Our company came out of Y Combinator in 2015. Since then we've grown to 1000+ remote workers, with strong venture-backing (including Sequoia Capital) and over $30M in funding to date. We are fully remote across Asia and US time zones.
  • Check out Magic's Business Profile
  • Know more about our Team via Magic's Careers Page﻿﻿
Why This Role Was Made For You
If you've spent years making cold calls, grinding pipelines from zero, and converting skeptics into buyers — you're exactly who we're looking for.

Magic gives you 50+ warm inbound leads every month. No cold calling, no list-building, no prospecting from scratch. Your skills — the discipline, the persistence, the ability to handle rejection without flinching — are the exact thing our warm leads need on the other end of the phone.
What You'll Get
The Account Executive role, with one key difference: every lead is inbound and warm.No cold outreach required.
  • Top performers hit 80–150% of monthly target consistently
  • At 100% quota: $3,500–$4,500/month
  • At 150%+: $5,000+/month
  • Paid monthly, in USD, regardless of where you're based

Our Hiring Process
  1. Quick Screen + Video Assessment (4 dropdown questions + 3 short video prompts, no live call)
  2. HR Background Check (45-minute call)
  3. Sales Leadership Interview + Live Role Play + Final Panel
  4. Offer within 48 hours of final stage

What Winning Looks Like
  • 2–8 inbound discovery calls a day, never dropping a follow-up
  • 15+ quality discovery calls per week with C-level and Director-level prospects
  • Every "not now" treated as a future win — patient, creative, persistent
  • CRM always clean, next steps always set
  • Quota hit monthly, with eyes on exceeding it

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the full sales cycle — from inbound discovery call through close and onboarding handoff
  • Uncover pain, establish urgency, match the right Magic product to each prospect's needs
  • Manage a high-volume pipeline with discipline
  • Collaborate with Support and Ops so clients start strong and stay happy
  • Treat coaching as part of the job — apply feedback fast

Your Background

You Are the Right Fit If You've Done Any of These:
  • Outbound sales — cold calling, SDR/BDR with a track record of booking and closing, field sales, door-to-door, telesales
  • B2C closing — insurance, real estate, financial products, automotive, telecom, retail finance. You closed deals face-to-face or over the phone, and you hit numbers.
  • BPO sales — outbound or upselling roles at a call center with U.S. client exposure
  • SDR/BDR promoted to AE — you've already made the jump, or you're ready to make it now
  • Any sales role where rejection was part of the job and you showed up anyway

What We Need From You
  • English at C1 or C2 — clear, confident, natural with U.S. buyers
  • Proven track record of hitting or exceeding targets — any industry, B2B or B2C
  • CRM discipline — HubSpot or equivalent
  • Available Monday–Friday during US Eastern or Central hours
  • Stable home internet (min. 40 Mbps) for daily video calls
  • Mindset: Hungry · Gritty · Coachable · Accountable

This Role Is NOT For You If: You wait for a manager to tell you what to do each day. You treat "not now" as a dead end. You blame leads or tools when numbers fall short. You see CRM hygiene as optional admin work.

What's in it for you

Your Offer
  • Guaranteed Base - $1,500 – $2,500 monthly foundation for stability
  • Performance Commission - 15–25%, increasing with performance excellence
  • Average Commission Reality - $1,500 – $2,000 monthly (what most AEs earn)
  • Total Monthly Earnings - $2,500 – $4,500+ with a clear path to increase
  • Truly Uncapped Commission - Our top performers consistently earn $5,000+ monthly
  • Employment Type - Independent Contractor/Consultant – Full-Time
  • Workplace Type - Fully Remote
  • Reporting To - Inbound Sales Manager

Your Growth Path
  • Account Executive (0–6 months): Master Magic’s product suite, build pipeline discipline, establish consultative selling habits
  • Senior Account Executive (6–18 months): Consistently exceed quota, mentor new AEs, manage higher-value accounts
  • Team Lead / Sales Manager (18–36 months): Lead a pod of AEs, own team targets, contribute to sales strategy
  • Sales Director (3+ years): Oversee sales operations, drive go-to-market strategy, partner with leadership on growth

Key Time Zone Schedule Requirements
  • Work Schedule: 9-hour shifts following US business hours
  • Paid Training Schedule: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM Eastern Time (mandatory attendance for 5 weeks)
  • Time Zone Alignment: Must be able to consistently work in Eastern Time, including adjustments for Daylight Saving Time and other US time zones
  • Availability: Monday to Friday, with consistent availability during U.S. business hours

Equipment Requirements (Self-Provided)
  • Computer/laptop meeting company specifications
  • Reliable high-speed internet connection (minimum 50 Mbps download / 10 Mbps upload)
  • Professional headset for clear client communication
  • Quiet, distraction-free work environment—all calls and interviews must be conducted from a professional, stationary setup (not while walking or commuting)
  • Backup power/internet solution for uninterrupted client service
You've fought for every deal you've ever closed. These leads are yours. Apply now.
﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿

raw.excerpt: Calling all innovators – find your future at Fiserv.
raw.description:
Calling all innovators – find your future at Fiserv.

We’re Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants, and consumers to one another millions of times a day – quickly, reliably, and securely. Any time you swipe your credit card, pay through a mobile app, or withdraw money from the bank, we’re involved. If you want to make an impact on a global scale, come make a difference at Fiserv.

Job Title

Merchant Account Executive - US Remote + 50%+ Travel

What does a successful Merchant Account Executive do?

In this dynamic and rewarding role, a successful Merchant Account Executive will be responsible for a portfolio of Community Financial Institutions of varying size and complexity. You will enjoy developing strategic growth plans and drive retention with the financial institution at multiple levels of leadership, including executive leadership up to CEOs. You will thrive in the client’s office, driving lasting results and relationship longevity. Lastly, a successful Merchant Account Executive will increase satisfaction and loyalty for current clients while optimizing and protecting revenue.

What you will do:

  • Reach across Fiserv to solve complex issues as well as participate in strategic and tactical initiatives for continued efficiency, with a strong focus on delivery of results.
  • Partner closely with our internal support teams to ensure we are aligned on the objectives and meeting expectations of the client.
  • Ensure client retention and controlling renewal compression to limit the erosion of pricing at renewal.
  • Build, foster, and maintain client relationships to improve visibility of additional company solutions and develop further growth opportunities.
  • Conduct client training, metric performance discussions, and serving as an escalation point.

What you will need to have:

  • 6+ years of selling experience in merchant services
  • 2+ years of managing a portfolio of clients
  • Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, work, and/or military experience

What would be great to have:

  • 1+ year work experience in a financial institution (bank or credit union)
  • Experience with Salesforce, eCRM, Microsoft Office
  • High proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint, PowerBI

Important info about this role:

  • Ability to travel a minimum of 50% of the time and work weekends/evenings, as necessary

Perks at work:

  • We’re #FiservProud of our commitment to your overall well-being with a growing offering of physical, mental, emotional, and financial benefits from day one.
  • Maintain a healthy work-life balance with paid holidays, generous time off policies, including Unlimited Recharge & Refuel for qualifying associates, and free counseling through our EAP.
  • Plan for your future with competitive salaries, the Fiserv 401(k) Savings Plan, and our Employee Stock Purchase Plan.
  • Recognize and be recognized by colleagues with our Living Proof program where you can exchange points for a variety of rewards.
  • Prioritize your health with a variety of medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance options and a range of well-being resources through our Fuel Your Life program.
  • Advance your career with training, development, certification, and internal mobility opportunities.
  • Join Employee Resource Groups that promote our diverse and inclusive culture where associates can share perspectives, exchange ideas, and elevate careers.

This role is not eligible to be performed in Colorado, California, District of Columbia, Hawaii, Illinois, Massachusetts, Maryland, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, Nevada, Rhode Island, Vermont, Virginia, Maine or Washington.


It is unlawful to discriminate against a prospective employee due to the individual's status as a veteran.

Please note that salary ranges provided for this role on external job boards are salary estimates made by outside parties and may not be accurate.

Thank you for considering employment with Fiserv. Please:

  • Apply using your legal name
  • Complete the step-by-step profile and attach your resume (either is acceptable, both are preferable).

Our commitment to Equal Opportunity:

Fiserv is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, protected veteran status, or any other category protected by law.

If you have a disability and require a reasonable accommodation in completing a job application or otherwise participating in the overall hiring process, please contact . Please note our AskHR representatives do not have visibility to your application status. Current associates who require a workplace accommodation should refer to Fiserv’s Disability Accommodation Policy for additional information.

Note to agencies:

Fiserv does not accept resume submissions from agencies outside of existing agreements. Please do not send resumes to Fiserv associates. Fiserv is not responsible for any fees associated with unsolicited resume submissions.

Warning about fake job posts:

Please be aware of fraudulent job postings that are not affiliated with Fiserv. Fraudulent job postings may be used by cyber criminals to target your personally identifiable information and/or to steal money or financial information. Any communications from a Fiserv representative will come from a legitimate Fiserv email address.
